Priya: quick heads-up — bringing up petrel-embed-v1 with int6 quant showed a weird cluster split for phonetic queries (e.g., 'alpha' vs 'alfa'). Low cost wins but quality hit on that subset. @Kevin can you eyeball when you have a minute? :eyes:
Kevin: on it. can you paste the recall@1/5/10 for both the full holdout and the phonetic subset so i have numbers to chew on?
Priya: sure — full holdout vs phonetic subset (quant6 run):
```
holdout   recall@1: 0.83  recall@5: 0.95  recall@10: 0.97
phonetic  recall@1: 0.62  recall@5: 0.78  recall@10: 0.85
model: petrel-embed-v1  dim=768  quant=6 (per-tensor)
```
Anne: that's a pretty big drop on phonetic. was the fp16 baseline similar across both?
Priya: fp16 baseline (previous run):
```
holdout   recall@1: 0.81  recall@5: 0.95  recall@10: 0.97
phonetic  recall@1: 0.80  recall@5: 0.92  recall@10: 0.95
```
Priya: so int6 hurts phonetic specifically (recall@1 from 0.80 -> 0.62).
Kevin: interesting — suggests phonetic similarity depends on small angular differences. possibilities: quantization pre/post-normalization mismatch, per-tensor scaling too coarse, or cosine vs dot normalization behavior changed. can you share a quick UMAP of the failing set?
Priya: uploaded a quick UMAP snapshot to the eval bucket; phonetic group splits into two clusters, one cluster shifted and lower norm by ~0.12. quick run command i used: `python eval.py --model petrel-embed-v1 --quant 6 --subset phonetic`
embed-bot: CI: eval run 1716161650 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/petrel/1716161650/ (umap.png, recall_table.csv, sample_pairs.json)
Anne: try per-channel quantization (per-channel int6) — often preserves directionality for dense kernels. also check whether we quantized before normalization: quantizing pre-norm vectors can amplify tiny errors. if encoder uses `normalize=True` post-embedding, re-run quantization after normalization.
Kevin: i'll spin a quick per-channel int6 ONNX export later today and compare cosine distributions (fp16 vs q6 tensor vs q6 channel). Priya, can you add 20 contrastive phonetic pairs that failed? i'll use them as a focused QA set.
Priya: added 20 pairs to s3://redwood-evals/petrel/phonetic_pairs_171616/ and linked a patch with eval config. also observed np.std diff: `np.std(np.linalg.norm(vecs_fp16 - vecs_q6, axis=1)) ~ 0.047` on the phonetic subset (higher than expected).
Anne: :thumbsup: proposed triage plan:
1) Run per-channel int6 quant and compare recall distribution on phonetic set.
2) Run quantization after L2-normalize (post-norm quant) and compare.
3) Try clipping activation ranges (narrower dynamic range) to reduce outlier scale shifts.
4) If still bad, consider a phonetic route: fallback to fp16 for requests detected as phonetic via small classifier or token heuristic.
Kevin: sounds good. i'll take (1) and (2) today, will post results here.
Priya: thanks — i'll coordinate runs (3) and add the failing sample list. will update thread with new recall table and UMAP. ping me if you need direct access to the eval infra.
Anne: thanks team. reconvene tomorrow after kernel tests.
